newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ occupancy rates fall slightly in February - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ occupancy rates fall slightly in February - SNZ.

text.p: Accommodation occupancy decreased slightly from January 1997 to February 1997 to 41.3 percent, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
"This reflects the expected drop in summer holiday makers at caravan parks and camping grounds," SNZ said.
"However, this was offset to some extent by the increase in business-related travel after the January holiday period."
Motels had the highest occupancy rate at 69.0 percent, up from the January figure of 63.4 percent. Hotels recorded the largest increase in occupancy, rising to 65.3 percent from 50.1 percent.
Caravan parks and camping grounds was the only accommodation type to record a decrease in occupancy in February, falling to 16.9 percent from 29.1 percent in January.
The national occupancy rate excluding caravan parks and camping grounds was 64.9 percent, up from 55.6 percent in January, SNZ said.
